subject.title: Discord compaction still fails with provider_error_4xx after #90496 closure on 2026.6.5

question: For Discord sessions that hit provider_error_4xx during Codex budget compaction, should OpenClaw rotate/preserve the transcript into a fresh usable session, surface an auth/provider recovery path, or fail without automatic recovery?
rationale: Current source shows the failure is still routed through the Codex-native compaction boundary, but choosing automatic rotation versus explicit provider/auth recovery changes session-state semantics and user-visible Discord behavior.

options.title: Choose recovery policy here
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical tracker, require live current-main Discord/Codex proof, and implement the chosen provider-4xx recovery behavior with regression tests.

options.title: Fold into timeout work
options.body: Treat the symptom as covered by the timeout partial-progress tracker, accepting that Codex HTTP 403 recovery may remain unowned if the timeout PR lands alone.

options.title: Close as already fixed
options.body: Treat the merged context-engine ownership fix as sufficient, despite the reporter's 2026.6.6 retest and current source still showing the provider-4xx recovery gap.

recommendation.title: Choose recovery policy here
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical tracker, require live current-main Discord/Codex proof, and implement the chosen provider-4xx recovery behavior with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged follow-up fixed adjacent Codex/session ownership paths and clearly documented the provider_error_4xx recovery gap as out of scope.
